elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to each Party.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 applies to “each Party” and expressly states that the cap is mutual.

elements.element: The fee-based limb uses all fees paid or payable under the Agreement, without being limited to the Implementation Fee or first Order Form.
elements.evidence: Although Section 21.1 refers to Fees under the Agreement, Section 1.5 defines “Fees” exclusively as the Implementation Fee, and Section 1.6 fixes that one-time fee at USD 12,000. The edit therefore does not capture other fees paid or payable under the Agreement.

elements.element: The fee-based limb is measured over the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 measures the period preceding “the event giving rise to the claim,” not the claim itself. Those dates can differ.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the applicable 12-month fee amount and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 expressly applies the greater of its fee-based limb and USD 1,000,000, although the fee-based limb is substantively narrowed by the definition of Fees.

elements.element: Neither Party is liable for indirect damages, subject to the stated carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 mutually excludes indirect damages except for Excluded Claims, to the extent legally excludable.

elements.element: Neither Party is liable for consequential damages, subject to the stated carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 mutually excludes consequential damages except for Excluded Claims, to the extent legally excludable.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes a Party’s breach of confidentiality obligations in Excluded Claims, and Section 21.1 excludes those claims from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data-protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes breach of data-protection obligations in Excluded Claims, which are outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes breach of security obligations in Excluded Claims, which are outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes indemnification obligations in Excluded Claims, which are outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes gross negligence in Excluded Claims, which are outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes wilful misconduct in Excluded Claims, which are outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Liability for fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes fraud in Excluded Claims, which are outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Liability for infringement of the other Party’s intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes infringement or misappropriation of the other Party’s intellectual property in Excluded Claims, which are outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Customer’s payment obligations are not damages for purposes of the liability cap.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 protects only Customer’s obligation to pay “undisputed Fees for conforming Services.” It does not state that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.

elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to each Party.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 applies to “each Party” and expressly states that the cap is mutual.

elements.element: The cap amount is equal to 12 months’ fees.
elements.evidence: The operative cap is the greater of the defined Fees for the lookback period and USD 1,000,000, not a cap equal to 12 months’ fees. In addition, “Fees” is defined solely as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Breach of confidentiality obligations is an Excluded Claim and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is an Excluded Claim and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is an Excluded Claim and therefore outside the Section 21.1 cap.

result.reason: The redline adds the USD 1,000,000 floor and retains mutuality, the damages exclusion, and all requested carve-outs. However, the unchanged definition of “Fees” still limits the fee limb to the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, so replacing “first Order Form” with “under this Agreement” does not achieve the stated fee-base expansion. The lookback runs from the event giving rise to the claim rather than the claim, and the payment-obligation protection is limited to undisputed Fees for conforming Services. No complete preferred or fallback level is achieved, although unrelated commercial terms are preserved.
